To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Dirac procedure does not exhaustively pick out the matter theories of general relativity and that the universal light cone of special relativity does not necessarily emerge from the relational premises.

1) relationalism alone does not exhaustively pick out general relativity as the only theory of geometrodynamics, 2) relationalism alone is compatible with equivalence principle violating matter, and 3) relationalism alone may not even be compatible with the special relativity principle of the universal light-cone.

1) there are no first principles from which one can exhaustively pick out the Dirac procedure's general relativity, and 2) that the matter results and conjectured results that were previously thought to be consequences of relational first principles are contingent upon additional unrelational simplicity premises.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question whether the relational first principles are sufficient for the Dirac procedure to pick out the geometrodynamical theory corresponding to general relativistic physics, or whether the relational first principle is not sufficient for the Diric procedure to exhaustively pick out general relativistic physics.
the question of how far one can go in the direction of a relational first principle for physics, and the answer so far has been: not quite so far as previously thought.
a program of finding a first principles basis for physics that is as simple as possible, but not simpler, and in this paper we find a number of ways in which the program can be further simplified.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Dirac procedure does not exhaustively pick out general relativity with a particular kind of matter theory, namely one that respects the equivalence principle.
the Dirac procedure is a very powerful tool for picking out geometrodynamics, but that the matter theories and other features it picks out are not as robust as it was previously held.
the relational first principles alone do not exhaustively pick out the geometrodynamical theory, but they can be supplemented with a number of unrelational simplicity principles to do so.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relationalist program has made a lot of progress in picking out the dynamics of general relativity, but it remains to be seen whether the matter theories that are also exhaustively picked out by the program are as simple and as physically interesting as the relationalist program would hope.
the Dirac procedure with matter is slower than previously thought, that it is not exhaustive, and that the results and conjectures that it does produce are not as general as previously thought.
relational premises are sufficient for geometrodynamics with matter, but that they do not suffice for the full set of matter theories and principles of physics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Dirac procedure, while it exhaustively picks out general relativity, is contingent upon further assumptions that are unrelational and thus not in the spirit of relationalism.
relationalism is a powerful but not sufficient basis for geometrodynamics and its matter theories.
the Dirac procedure is not a complete theory selection method.
